page: The OVHcloud r2-60 is a memory-optimized virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel x86_64 processor based on the Haswell architecture, running at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz with one thread per core. The instance is equipped with 60 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 15 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 100 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates that the r2-60 is positioned for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity rather than raw processing power. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is recorded at 868.79, while multi-core performance reaches 3118.23, both falling into the lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only large block speed of 19.87 GB/sec and a write speed of 15.43 GB/sec, though the Passmark memory score achieves an average rating. Redis SET operations perform at 4.42 million operations per second.

From a resource density perspective, the r2-60 offers qualitative cost efficiency for applications that are bound by memory capacity rather than CPU throughput. Because it utilizes an older processor architecture with moderate benchmark scores, it avoids the premium costs associated with high-frequency compute instances. This makes the server well-suited for caching layers, in-memory databases, and memory-intensive background workers that do not demand high-performance computing.
